mechanism.domainTask: CAD reconstruction and n-dimensional ball partitioning via OpenEvolve
mechanism.populationDetail: OpenEvolve maintains multiple parallel sub-populations/islands; the applied configuration uses three islands with periodic migration, while each island uses the MAP-Elites archive.
mechanism.archiveDetail: MAP-Elites preserves elite programs in a discretized feature space using dimensions such as program complexity and functional diversity (or task-specific descriptors).
mechanism.replacementDetail: The paper inherits OpenEvolve's archive and island implementation and describes it at framework level rather than providing complete archive-admission pseudocode.
mechanism.generationDetail: One high-quality parent program is rewritten; early generations make broad structural mutations while later generations make small localized parameter refinements.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The seven component scores, validity/error signals, and evaluator feedback are reused to guide subsequent code mutations; feedback detail is partly inherited from OpenEvolve.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: One high-quality parent is selected from an island's MAP-Elites/archive state; exact score/rank sampling and migration ordering are inherited or under-specified.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: An application-level combination of MAP-Elites, island migration, static small/large model mixtures, and geometry-specific approximate multi-metric evaluation; the observed structural-discovery/parametric-refinement transition is not a formal controller.

provenance.citationWarning: The current survey cites Applied AlphaEvolve under Staged Evaluation, but the paper does not describe early candidate screening; it directly supports Approximate Evaluation through voxelized and sampled geometric metrics. Archive admission, parent sampling, and verbalized feedback details are partly inherited from OpenEvolve and should remain medium-confidence.
